title: Linux Security Hardening
summary: A systematic overview of Linux server hardening across five areas: authentication, access control, security auditing, resource control, and intrusion prevention. Covers key configuration files including /etc/login.defs, sshd_config, and rsyslog.conf.

title: Cybersecurity Law of the People's Republic of China
summary: Full text of the Cybersecurity Law of the PRC across seven chapters and seventy-nine articles, covering network operation security, critical information infrastructure protection, network information security, monitoring and early warning, emergency response, and legal liability.

title: Cybersecurity Tools
summary: A curated list of dozens of classic security tools — Nessus, Wireshark, Metasploit, Nmap, Burp Suite, and more — with their functional positioning and use cases, covering vulnerability scanning, sniffing, penetration testing, and password cracking.

title: Information Gathering Workflow
summary: Enterprise-grade penetration testing information gathering workflow: from scanner probing, DNS zone transfer vulnerabilities, subdomain brute-force, ICP record lookup, and SSL status checks to app decompilation and Google/Baidu dorking.

title: Level Protection Workflow
summary: End-to-end workflow for cybersecurity level protection assessment: define objectives, gather information, detect vulnerabilities, verify findings, analyze information, determine requirements, organize data, and produce the report — with key points for each phase.

title: Nmap Reference Guide
summary: An annotated Chinese-language reference for the official Nmap documentation, covering host discovery, port scanning techniques (SYN/ACK/UDP/FIN/Xmas, etc.), service version detection, OS fingerprinting, firewall evasion, and output formats.

title: Reverse Engineering Tools
summary: A roundup of mainstream reverse engineering and decompilation tools — IDA, OllyDbg, x64dbg, JAD, dotPeek, dnSpy, radare2, and more — covering Java, .NET, Android, and native binary platforms.

title: Spring Boot Framework Integration (Part 1)
summary: A Spring Boot + spring-data-jpa + MySQL framework integration tutorial covering project creation, pom.xml configuration, application.properties database setup, and Bean/Controller/Repository/Service layer code samples.

title: Spring Boot Framework Integration (Part 2)
summary: Building on the previous framework, this adds logback-spring logging configuration. Covers Spring Boot default logging behavior, custom logback-spring.xml (console/file/error log separation), and debug/release environment switching.

title: IDE and Editor Roundup
summary: A categorized roundup of mainstream IDEs and editors by language: JetBrains suite, VS Code, Eclipse, IntelliJ IDEA, PyCharm, CLion, WebStorm, and more, plus a dedicated section on reverse engineering tools (IDA/ILSpy/dotPeek).

title: Tag Plugins Plus & Kmark Syntax
summary: Comprehensive usage documentation for the Butterfly theme tag plugin, covering syntax, parameters, and style previews for 20+ tags including tip, note, folding, timeline, checkbox, radio, link, ghcard, btns, sites, gallery, and progress.

title: Battery-Powered Wireless Keyboard & Mouse Buying Guide
summary: From popular battery-powered wireless mice (Logitech G304/G603, Razer Basilisk X/DeathAdder V2 X, SteelSeries Rival 3 Wireless) to keyboards (IKBC, GANSS, Lofree, HHKB), with model, connection type, battery specs, and hands-on impressions for each.

title: Monitor Buying Guide
summary: A programmer's perspective on the ten key monitor parameters: size vs. viewing distance, resolution ratios, refresh rate, response time, color gamut/depth/accuracy, ports (HDMI/DP/Type-C), panel types (IPS/VA/TN), and sync technologies.

title: National Food Standards Reference
summary: A reference of national execution standard numbers (GB/GB/T) for common food categories — cooking oil, salt, vinegar, rice, soy sauce, tea (black/oolong/green/dark/white/yellow), frozen desserts, alcoholic beverages, and more — for easy lookup and comparison.

title: Troubleshooting a Friend's Potato PC for FFXIV
summary: A real troubleshooting log: a friend's FFXIV ran at only 20 FPS. Task Manager showed 100% CPU usage but the clock was stuck at 1.99 GHz (base 2.5 GHz). Remote diagnosis revealed the laptop wasn't plugged in, causing thermal throttling. Three solutions were offered: reinstall the game, play in fullscreen mode, or get a new PC.
